stories.summary: Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre secured overwhelming support at the party's Calgary convention, winning 87.4% in a mandatory leadership review following his 2025 election loss. The result cements his position despite recent caucus defections to the Liberals.

stories.summary: Prime Minister Carney signed an auto deal with South Korea and announced plans to visit India in March for trade agreements on uranium, energy and AI. The moves are part of his strategy to double non-US exports within a decade as tensions with Trump escalate.

stories.headline: Bank of Canada holds interest rate at 2.25% amid trade uncertainty
stories.summary: The Bank of Canada kept its benchmark rate steady at 2.25% for the second consecutive meeting, citing elevated geopolitical uncertainty and upcoming USMCA trade negotiations. Governor Tiff Macklem warned that monetary policy cannot fully offset potential tariff damage.

stories.summary: Prime Minister Carney's speech at Quebec City describing the 1759 Battle of Plains of Abraham as symbolizing a 'partnership' between two peoples drew fierce criticism from the Parti Québécois and Bloc Québécois, who accused him of rewriting history. Carney refused to apologize.

stories.summary: Prime Minister Carney unveiled the Canadian Groceries and Essentials Benefit, expanding the GST credit to provide relief for rising food costs. The package also includes measures for food security and affordability as the government faces opposition pressure over cost of living.

stories.summary: The federal NDP confirmed five candidates for its March leadership convention: Rob Ashton, Tanille Johnston, Avi Lewis, Heather McPherson and Tony McQuail. Lewis leads in fundraising after the party lost official status following Singh's resignation post-election defeat.

stories.headline: US ambassador warns NORAD could change if Canada abandons F-35 purchase
stories.summary: US Ambassador Pete Hoekstra warned that NORAD would have to be 'altered' if Canada pulls back from its planned purchase of 88 F-35 fighter jets, saying the US would need to fly more aircraft into Canadian airspace. The State Department later clarified the comments amid continental defence concerns.

stories.summary: The Parti Québécois held its annual convention in Saint-Hyacinthe with Bloc Québécois leader Yves-François Blanchet offering support ahead of Quebec's fall election. Leaders accused Carney of launching the referendum campaign and renewed ties between federal and provincial sovereigntist parties.

stories.headline: Canadian Armed Forces member dies in Latvia deployment
stories.summary: A Canadian Armed Forces member died while deployed in Latvia as part of Operation Reassurance, the CAF's largest overseas mission. The deceased was Master Corporal Cristian Halmagean, based at 5th Canadian Division Support Base Gagetown, who had served nearly three years.
